title: hetzner-mcp connection config (v1)
$comment: HAND-WRITTEN MIRROR of connectionSchema/configFileSchema in src/config/schema.ts. zod-to-json-schema is deliberately not a dependency, so the two are kept in sync by a parity test that feeds the same fixtures to both: any property, default, bound or pattern changed in schema.ts must be changed here in the same commit. This file is published in the npm package (see package.json files[]) and is what a user's $schema key points at.

$schema.description: Points at this file so editors can validate and autocomplete the config.

defaultConnection.description: Connection used when a tool call does not name one. $HETZNER_CONNECTION overrides it. With exactly one connection it is unnecessary; with several and none designated, tools require an explicit connection.

extends.description: Path to a base config file, resolved relative to this file ('~/' is expanded). Exactly one level: the base file may not itself extend another. A name defined in both files replaces the base entry whole — there is no field-level merge.

connections.description: A connection is (surface, credential). A Cloud token is created inside one project and cannot see any other, so a second project is a second connection; the surface extends the same mechanism to the account-scoped API and to Robot.

connectionName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit, 31 characters max. The name maps to env vars by uppercasing and replacing - with _: 'acme-ops' <-> HETZNER_TOKEN_ACME_OPS.

command.description: Argv array executed WITHOUT a shell; trimmed stdout is the secret. No string splitting, no interpolation, no glob expansion. Example: ["op", "read", "op://Infra/hetzner/credential"].

keychainRef.description: Platform credential store: macOS `security find-generic-password`, Linux `secret-tool lookup`, Windows user-scoped DPAPI ciphertext at %LOCALAPPDATA%\hetzner-mcp\credentials.dat (not Credential Manager — no first-party CLI returns a generic credential's secret).

connection.$comment: There is no 'token', 'user' or 'password' property, and additionalProperties is false, so a literal credential here is a schema validation error rather than a discouraged option. There is no 'baseUrl' either: it is derived from 'surface'. Both are enforcement, not documentation.
connection.description: hetzner-mcp never stores credentials in config files. Point at a credential with tokenEnv/tokenCommand/tokenKeychain (cloud, hetzner) or userEnv+passwordEnv/userEnv+passwordCommand/credentialKeychain (robot), or set none of them and the conventional environment variables for the surface are read.

surface.description: Which Hetzner API this connection speaks to. cloud = api.hetzner.cloud/v1, bearer, scoped to ONE project. hetzner = api.hetzner.com/v1, bearer, account-scoped. robot = robot-ws.your-server.de, HTTP Basic, dedicated servers. The base URL is derived from this and is never configurable: Hetzner runs exactly one instance of each API, so a user-supplied URL could only repeat what is already known, or be wrong.

label.description: Human label shown in doctor output and error messages.

tokenEnv.description: cloud/hetzner only. Name of the environment variable holding the API token.

tokenCommand.description: cloud/hetzner only. Argv array whose stdout is the API token.

tokenKeychain.description: cloud/hetzner only. Credential store item whose secret is the API token.

userEnv.description: robot only. Name of the environment variable holding the Robot web-service user (looks like '#123456+ws'). Set together with passwordEnv or passwordCommand.

passwordEnv.description: robot only. Name of the environment variable holding the Robot web-service password.

passwordCommand.description: robot only. Argv array whose stdout is the Robot web-service password.

credentialKeychain.description: robot only, and it carries BOTH halves: the item's 'account' is the Robot web-service user and its secret is the password. One item per login is what keeps the user — half a credential — out of this file.

readOnly.description: Refuse every write and destructive operation on this connection regardless of token scope. $HETZNER_READ_ONLY=true forces this on for all connections; it can only tighten, never loosen.

allowDestructive.description: Per-connection override of $HETZNER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE, ANDed with it. It can only narrow: true here grants nothing on a server where the global flag is off, while false keeps this connection protected on a server where it is on.

allOf.$comment: At most one credential source: two sources means two answers to 'where is the credential' and no rule for which wins.
A source from the wrong surface is not a typo the user can see: tokenEnv on a robot connection reads as sensible right up to the 401.
